$comment: Six category circuits, rebuilt for replay and reach in data/season_fun_rebuild.json with the measurements in data/fun_audit.json. Catalogue evidence is not a substitute for human difficulty and enjoyment playtesting.

Dynamic Clicking.description: The targets are moving, so stay on each one for a split second until you're sure you're on it before you click, and don't let a sudden change of direction drag your crosshair with it. On targets that take several hits, move with them until the last click.

families.why: Keeps Pasu in the circuit on the lineage players actually play: its Novice and Intermediate rungs have about thirty-five times the players of the Pasu rungs they replace (fun_audit.json reach). Slow introduces it, small halves the target, and the reactive edit makes the small targets react. The Reload edit, which more benchmarks name, is left out because it runs 86 seconds (50 local runs, 84% agreement in scenario_durations.json).
Targets on a fixed path, so it's more about timing than reading. Easy and Hard S1 are from Aimerz+ S1; Normal and Hard are the older S0 cuts.

Bouncing-target clicking from two authors. SuperbAim's BounceClick for the first two rungs, then Sparky's and rAim's Bounce 180, where the balls really bounce and a reload replaces the accuracy penalty. The order between the two authors hasn't been playtested.
Targets strafe around you and move up and down, so it's wider than Pasu. psalmTS angelic click and Pasu Angelic, each with a larger-target cut below it.
Trims the circuit's Pasu-style families from four to three, the source of most complaints about luck deciding a run. Tamspeed's author publishes the ladder as named tiers, so the order is his.

Popcorn with a reload instead of accuracy scoring. rAim's Goated easy cut with double-size targets, then rAim Easy, Sparky's version where the bots bounce, and Goated rAim with 10% smaller bots for Expert.

Floating Heads Timing 400% is the original the Floating Heads family was built from; its Novice and Intermediate rungs have eight times the players and more than twice the replay of the family it replaces. Larger introduces it; FIXED removes a frame-rate speed inconsistency and locks field of view; Extra Small Speed shrinks the head and speeds it up. The FIXED Extra Small edit was the natural Expert rung but its board is under the floor the Expert window sets for a board its ranks are cut from.
rungs: Floating Heads Timing Extra Small Speed

families.why: Far moving dots at several vertical layers turn the run into a layered gallery. The Goated Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert edits retain the same scene while changing the challenge.
Adds arcing movement the circuit lacked and replaces one of its least replayed families. Voltaic's own tiers set the order; the Expert rung is the 20% smaller edit of Advanced.

CatClick is graded by Viscose in all four of its tiers, Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert, so the family is one scenario's own four cuts with no handover between authors, and its two easier cuts carry some of the busiest boards in the pool. Its author description says nothing about the mechanic; the season files it where Viscose does, under dynamic clicking.

Precise Tracking.description: Stay smooth and keep your crosshair in the middle of the target the whole time, moving with it in one steady motion and using your arm on long strafes. If your aim gets shaky or you keep losing the target, drop to an easier version.

families.why: SmoothBot Invincible Goated at every rung instead of Voltaic's Smoothbot: 75% speed, Easy, the standard version, then the smaller cut for Expert. The bot can't die, so the whole run is time on target.

A dedicated horizontal centering test separates velocity matching from multidirectional control. Entry, Novice and Intermediate community cuts lead into the established no-strafes version. Apogee band names describe our progression, not the names of the source cuts. Exact target-size differences are not claimed; band handovers need playtesting.

cloverRawControl is named by eleven benchmarks, tied for the most of any scenario the season did not use, and its Easy edit by nine more. The previous PreciseTrack family started on a 293-entry leaderboard. Big, Easy and standard are the author's own steps; Expert is Viscose's hard edit, used because the author's Hard board is under the floor the Expert window sets.
Smooth with no blinks, going by the scenario description. 55% speed, 75%, full speed, then Extra Small for Expert.

SYW FIXED is replayed 47.6 times per player, one of the highest rates of any tracking scenario on KovaaK's. Easy and the original lock field of view; FIXED forces ADS to remove the cheese; Extra thin narrows the bot.
rungs: SYW (Smooth Your Wrist) FIXED Extra thin

families.why: A small dot that jumps gently and flies around you at changing distance and speed. Viscose's entry cut, then rAim's Easy at 90%, rAim Easy and rAim. The sheets file the top rung under Control Tracking, which this season grades as Precise.
The DVD-inspired moving target gives continuous tracking a recognizable screen-bounce motif. MASSIVE, Big, standard and Small keep the motion theme while reducing the target size.

PGTI is named by ten benchmarks and comes up again and again in community lists of favourite tracking scenarios. Easy 80% slows the Easy cut; Slower 80% slows the standard one; the standard edit is last. The Gold edit is left out because its bot is enlarged from Easy, which would put an easier scenario above a harder one.
A gently jumping dot flying around the player adds a flowing orbital chase. Viscose's Horizontal Entry, Easier, standard and Hard cuts expand the motion challenge while keeping the same visual theme.

waldoTS is one of the most-played tracking scenarios in the catalogue, with 3.7 million plays on its standard cut. Viscose grades its Novice, Intermediate, standard and Elite cuts as Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert, and AimSpeed grades the standard and Elite cuts too, so the progression is one scenario's own cuts.

Reactive Tracking.description: React to where the target goes instead of guessing, and sit slightly on the side it's moving away from so you have room when it turns. Stay relaxed, because jittery aim usually means you're tensing up, and if you catch yourself predicting, play an easier version for a while.

families.why: Sparky's Ground Plaza v3: six bots strafing on the ground at mixed lengths and distances. Easy, the standard version, OW with instant ground acceleration, then Thin for Expert.
Air Voltaic Invincible 4: one invincible bot changing direction in the air, nothing to kill. Viscose grades Entry, Easier and Medium; the full version is Expert.

Same skill, rebuilt on the Air Angelic 4 lineage whose Easy edit nine benchmarks use. The previous Novice and Intermediate rungs had leaderboards of 798 and 1,637 entries. The steps go from 80% speed to Easy, the standard edit, then the smaller bot.
The long-strafes lineage carries some of the highest replay in tracking. The ladder moves the bot from kinda far to midrange to close, then thins it, so difficulty grows along one visible axis.
rungs: Close long strafes invincible very thin

families.why: A target that leaps and strafes with mixed dodge profiles. wobin's Easier cut, then Aimerz+'s mid-range Leapstrafes Control Medium, then wobin's standard and Hard cuts. No sheet names a sub-skill for wobin's version, so putting it in Reactive is a judgement call.

rungs: Flicker Plaza rAim Easy Less Blinks
families.why: Recovery replaces a third mixed-air test. Kindaclose introduces random acceleration, slowing and stops; the three Flicker Plaza cuts then challenge reacquisition after teleports. This is a deliberate change of mechanic between Novice and Intermediate, not a shared-bot speed ladder. Less Blinks provides the transition.

Air Spectral's deliberately unusual Air movement adds a surprise-driven chase. Easy 85%, Easy, standard and Harder retain that theme. Its terse author description supports the unusual-motion intent, not a claim of measured enjoyment.

Air Divine-style movement brings a longer aerial course into the season. Easy Slowed, Easy, No UFO and Harder progress from a slowed course to the full challenge; the final UFO handover needs playtesting.
rungs: Air CELESTIAL No UFO Easy Slowed

families.why: Air Pure mixes bots with different dodge profiles in one air arena, so every target asks for a different read. Revosect's time-scored entry cut, six bots circling the player, leads into the Intermediate, standard and Hard cuts that Viscose and snakbox grade. The handover between the two editions needs playtesting.

A close strafing opponent adds a grounded duel-like chase beside the aerial courses. Easy Thin, standard, Thin and Precise+ are a proposed progression; speed and size both change, so the first handover needs playtesting.
rungs: Close Fast Strafes Easy Invincible - Thin

Speed Switching.description: Hold fire and get to the next target as fast as you can in a straight line, without flicking past it. Kill each target fully before you move, and start finding the next one while you finish the current one.

families.why: Static dot switching without Voltaic's cuts. wobin's Easy, which leans on horizontal spawns, for Novice, AimSpeed's Entry, the 30% larger cut, then plain DotTS, which Aimerz+ SpeedTS and AimSpeed both grade at Hard.

Large and standard range targets establish routing and clean transfers. Viscose Varied introduces progressively shrinking targets; rAim finishes with a smaller fixed-target challenge. Only the Advanced rung is an evolving task. This adapts the source routine's speed-to-precision idea across related variants without changing their native scoring or duration.
Four flying targets, about a quarter second each. Here so the category isn't just size variants of one range. Elite S5 is the Expert rung.

A long-standing switching classic whose NR edit six benchmarks name, with about twice the Novice and Intermediate players of PivoTS. Easy, standard and small are the author's sizes; Speed lowers time-to-kill and enlarges the heads for pure pace.
You hold fire on each target instead of tapping, and some cuts regen if you flick off early. The slow-kill option next to DotTS and EddieTS.
Spherical bots moving slowly side to side, tracked briefly to kill. psalmTS Voltaic is the Advanced rung and VT psalmTS Advanced is Expert.
Stationary Vox targets reward route choice and rapid full-auto clears without movement reading. Jumbo, standard, Small and xxSmall turn the room into a four-band switching sprint.

Wave Relay had the lowest replay in the season, under three plays per player. beanTS is named by eight benchmarks and has a board of over nine thousand players at every rung. Larger, standard and 30% smaller are target sizes; 200% doubles the speed.
Slow horizontal targets at several depths make a readable aerial switching gallery. Four published skyTS bands keep the movement predictable while increasing the target challenge.

Low-FOV target switching concentrates the action into short, fast clears. Easy, NR, rAim and NR Small are a proposed cross-edit progression; the two middle releases need an in-game difficulty comparison.

Evasive Switching.description: Focus on movement reading, sustained contact and clean transfers. Start with larger and slower targets, then add tighter movement, more distance and regeneration.

families.focus: Keep the crosshair on the bot through its direction changes. Switch after the kill.
families.why: Replace the mixed PureG/Aimerz progression with one published PasuTS lineage. Entry is explicitly 15% larger and 15% slower, with a short 20-hit clear; Intermediate, Advanced and Elite retain the task.

Floatswitch was the least replayed evasive family. patTargetSwitch is the original flick-and-track switching scenario and is not Voltaic, which keeps the Voltaic share of this category from growing. The Expert rung plays the same task while moving through a 360 room.

families.focus: Track the jump through the narrow space. Recenter before moving on.
families.why: Keep the narrow room and floating, gently jumping targets. Entry Speed combines larger, slower entry bots with a 25% shorter clear. Intermediate, Advanced and Elite keep their existing bands, so the easier start does not lower the upper-band challenge.

Hop Transfer was the second least replayed evasive family. Skeet Tracking has 386 thousand players at 31 plays each. 85% Speed slows it for Novice; Goated and Goated Small are the published harder edits.

families.focus: Track the bounce across the pentagon and choose the next target before the current one dies.
rungs: VT Penta Bounce Entry S5 Speed
families.why: Keep five bouncing targets and the pentagonal arena. Entry Speed adds bigger targets and 25% shorter time to kill to the slower Entry movement. Intermediate, Advanced and Elite keep their existing bands, so the easier start does not lower the upper-band challenge.

families.focus: Follow the full arc and hold the target through the finish as its depth changes.
families.why: Keep the curved B180T arena throughout. Begin with Easy Slower, then Easy, standard and finally Regen. Remove the Aimerz depth-pattern detour and postpone the regeneration penalty until Expert.

families.focus: Read the flight direction and make smooth transfers after each kill.
families.why: Entry Speed combines the published larger/slower Entry edit with larger targets and 25% shorter time to kill. Intermediate, Advanced and Elite keep their existing bands, so the easier start does not lower the upper-band challenge.

families.focus: Keep track of both chambers and move to the next target without dropping contact early.
families.why: Two stacked chambers add vertical route choices among four floating and jumping targets. The larger, slower Entry Speed variant shortens clears by 25%; Intermediate, Advanced and Elite retain one authored lineage. This replaces the mixed CB/Revosect Smooth Relay whose Expert board had only 145 sampled players and nearly tied top targets.

families.focus: Stay on the target until it dies. Any gap in damage gives health back.
families.why: Regenerating targets reward committed tracking after the flick. Entry and Intermediate use shorter time to kill; Control asks for longer contact; Hard adds bouncing. These are different training demands, not just faster versions. Unlike the retained Smooth family, the Control bots wiggle rather than circle.

families.focus: Control the strafe and keep contact through the kill. Switch after the target drops.
families.why: Easier explicitly makes bots bigger and slower with less punishing regeneration; Easy, standard and Hard continue the same named lineage. Replace the Avasive Expert edit: a lower record across different edits was not evidence of greater physical difficulty.

families.focus: Match the target's movement and keep contact through the regeneration window.
families.why: Use the authored Entry, Novice, Intermediate and Elite editions in ascending order. Remove Hard 30% Larger from Novice and the subsequent switch to non-bouncing Easy. Instant regeneration remains a commitment drill, so it comes late in the circuit; named editions are not measured difficulty equivalence.

Static Clicking.description: Your score is how little time passes between kills, so flick straight at each target, fix it with one small correction if you need to, and be looking at the next target before you click.

families.why: Original authored static circuit.

1wall 6targets small is the most played scenario on KovaaK's after the sandbox intro, 1.29 million players at 57 plays each, and the season had no member of its lineage. Jumbo introduces it, TE is the standard, small and extra small tighten the target without changing the rhythm.

5 Sphere Hipfire is a long-standing micro-flick staple; the Small edit alone has half a million players. The four rungs are one scenario at four target sizes, so the difficulty order is the author's own.

The previous Micro family had Novice and Intermediate leaderboards of 175 and 532 entries. RawMouseControlClicking3 is replayed 51.6 times per player, among the highest on KovaaK's. Reload Easy is 25% bigger, Reload removes accuracy scoring, Clicking3 restores it, and 30% smaller tightens it.
Original authored static circuit.
Original authored static circuit.
Original authored static circuit.

1w4ts Voltaic is named by four benchmarks and replayed 28.5 times per player, and the reload edits it grew are replayed nearly as often. The rungs step from larger targets through the Voltaic cut to the reload edits at smaller sizes.
Original authored static circuit.

Tile Frenzy is the scenario players describe as satisfying even when they concede it is easy, which is exactly the Novice job. Jumbo and standard carry the rhythm; Mini moves the wall far away so the same rhythm needs small movements; Extra mini is the smallest edit on a real board.

Vox's shooting-gallery layout offers route choice and quick successive kills. These Viscose click variants remove awkward spawns; Entry, Easier, Medium and Hard give the gallery a four-band progression.

Six-target reload clicking emphasizes a continuous clear-and-respawn rhythm. The first three cuts reduce target size; the Expert trustechain edit adds a different routing challenge. That final handover is a design choice requiring playtesting.
Three close static targets create short, repeatable chains with little travel time. Larger 80%, Larger, standard and 10% small provide a size progression for a compact score-chasing circuit.
